### Contributing guidelines

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [x] I have updated 'mini.nvim' to latest version of the `main` branch

### Module(s)

mini.completion

### Neovim version

0.11.x

### Description

unable to trigger completion in some cases

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b0dfe5ed-7aca-4dcf-801e-5ae14d525ade

I found that sometimes completion base str may start with '.', so items will be empty after calling 'process_items'

### Reproduction

1. Create separate 'nvim-repro' config directory:
    - '~/.config/nvim-repro/' on Unix
    - '~/AppData/Local/nvim-repro/' on Windows

2. Inside 'nvim-repro' directory create a file named 'init.lua'.
   Populate it with the following content:

    ```lua
    -- Clone latest 'mini.nvim' (requires Git CLI installed)
    vim.cmd('echo "Installing `mini.nvim`" | redraw')
    local mini_path = vim.fn.stdpath('data') .. '/site/pack/deps/start/mini.nvim'
    local clone_cmd = { 'git', 'clone', '--depth=1', 'https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim', mini_path }
    vim.fn.system(clone_cmd)
    vim.cmd('echo "`mini.nvim` is installed" | redraw')

    -- Make sure 'mini.nvim' is available
    vim.cmd('packadd mini.nvim')
    require('mini.deps').setup()

    -- Add extra setup steps needed to reproduce the behavior
    -- Use `MiniDeps.add('user/repo')` to install another plugin from GitHub
    ```

3. Run `NVIM_APPNAME=nvim-repro nvim` (i.e. execute `nvim` with `NVIM_APPNAME` environment variable set to "nvim-repro").
   Wait for all dependencies to install.

4. Replace this with description of interactive reproduction steps along with the behavior you observe.
   Feel free to include images/videos/etc, this helps a lot.

<details><summary>What to do after reporting an issue</summary>

After reporting the issue, it is safe (and even recommended for cleaner possible future bug reports) to remove 'nvim-repro' config from the system:
- Delete config directory ('~/.config/nvim-repro' on Unix).
- Delete data directory ('~/.local/share/nvim-repro' on Unix).
- Delete state directory ('~/.local/state/nvim-repro' on Unix).

</details>

comment_data.body: After I made the following simple modifications: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6b9a2a8a-95e7-477a-9d9b-a114de43ebed The autocomplete options display correctly, but the autocomplete list does not automatically appear when inserting more characters, and it exhibits strange behavior when manually triggered.

Thanks for the issue!

I did not (yet) have time to reproduce. Could you, please, elaborate on specific setup with which you could reproduce this? Are there any requirements for the project itself or just file test? If you could provide a copypasteable file text, that would also help.

I did manage to reproduce and unfortunately this is a consequence of how 'mini.completion' works with LSP.

The 'mini.completion' needs to compute the single base against which to filter early. It does so by first [looking at available completion candidates from the LSP server](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/dce9bc4e19d02d5c37fe71c16f40f8a5536b0386/lua/mini/completion.lua#L1864-L1868) in order to infer the column which should be a start of the completion "base" (i.e. which word is used to filter against suggested candidates).

The problem here is that in case of a `ptr1` almost all completion suggestions from `clangd` (and most importantly, the first one since 'mini.completion' ignores the rest here) contain `textEdit` that replaces the dot (with `textEdit` from column 6 to 7 and `newText` something like `->assign($0)`), *but* the `filterText` (what is used to filter completion candidates based on the current base to the left of cursor) value *do not* contain leading dot. This might be the case because there are couple of candidates that do not replace the dot (like by adding `use_count()`).

The `ptr2` doesn't have this problem since all suggested candidates do not remove the dot (i.e. `textEdit` is empty, from column 7 to column 7).

The #306 is relevant here.

---

The solution I can suggest here is to adjust how LSP items are processed only in 'cpp' files. For that:
- Create '~/.config/nvim/after/ftplugin/cpp.lua'.
- Add the following lines to it:

    ```lua
    vim.b.minicompletion_config = {
      lsp_completion = {
        process_items = function(items, base)
          -- Skip leading dot in base as items usually have `filterText` without it
          if base:sub(1, 1) == '.' then base = base:sub(2) end
          return MiniCompletion.default_process_items(items, base)
        end,
      },
    }
    ```

I am not sure if there are any other consequences here, but it works for this use case.

It does so by first [looking at available completion candidates from the LSP server](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/dce9bc4e19d02d5c37fe71c16f40f8a5536b0386/lua/mini/completion.lua#L1864-L1868) in order to infer the column which should be a start of the completion "base" (i.e. which word is used to filter against suggested candidates). > > The problem here is that in case of a `ptr1` almost all completion suggestions from `clangd` (and most importantly, the first one since 'mini.completion' ignores the rest here) contain `textEdit` that replaces the dot (with `textEdit` from column 6 to 7 and `newText` something like `->assign($0)`), _but_ the `filterText` (what is used to filter completion candidates based on the current base to the left of cursor) value _do not_ contain leading dot. This might be the case because there are couple of candidates that do not replace the dot (like by adding `use_count()`). > > The `ptr2` doesn't have this problem since all suggested candidates do not remove the dot (i.e. `textEdit` is empty, from column 7 to column 7). > > The [#306](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/issues/306) is relevant here. > > The solution I can suggest here is to adjust how LSP items are processed only in 'cpp' files. For that: > > * Create '~/.config/nvim/after/ftplugin/cpp.lua'. > * Add the following lines to it: > vim.b.minicompletion_config = { > lsp_completion = { > process_items = function(items, base) > -- Skip leading dot in base as items usually have `filterText` without it > if base:sub(1, 1) == '.' then base = base:sub(2) end > return MiniCompletion.default_process_items(items, base) > end, > }, > } > > I am not sure if there are any other consequences here, but it works for this use case. Thank you very much! But I found some other problems: completion items could show correctly when I type '.' but when I continue type 'g', the completion menu disappeared then I use \ to trigger it manually when I accept the first item 'get', the text inserted override the origin '.'

This is the next best thing I can propose here:

```lua
local process_items = function(items, base)
  -- If base starts with a dot, ensure that `filterText` of all items also
  -- starts with a dot. Otherwise they might be filtered out.
  if base:sub(1, 1) == '.' then
    for i = 1, #items do
      local filter_text = items[i].filterText
      if type(filter_text) == 'string' and filter_text:sub(1, 1) ~= '.' then
        items[i].filterText = '.' .. filter_text
      end
    end
  end

  return MiniCompletion.default_process_items(items, base)
end

vim.b.minicompletion_config = { lsp_completion = { process_items = process_items } }
```

But it still has issues and I am aware of that. This is all the consequence of `clangd` proposing completion candidates that have different `textEdit` regions (in this case - with or without replacing the `.`).

I'll take a look at what can be done here in 'mini.completion' itself. Maybe normalizing items to have the biggest `textEdit` region (by prepending/appending text to `newText` of less-than-the-biggest regions) is doable, but this will affect performance.

title: [mini.completion] completion issues with clangd
